title: Granular SLO-proportional evacuation with circuit hydration
creator: Leah Kim
description:
Problem: Active-active hosted API edge must be able to evacuate traffic from a degraded region while preserving streaming session continuity, protecting SLOs, and avoiding oscillatory circuit open/close behavior. We need a deterministic, telemetry-driven approach that proportionally bleeds traffic based on SLO headroom and circuit health rather than blunt all-or-nothing shifts.

Goal: Implement a SLO-proportional evacuation controller and a complementary "circuit hydration" workflow that (1) reduces traffic from impacted regions in fine-grained increments, (2) preserves in-flight streaming sessions with token-preserving handshakes or ephemeral proxies, (3) avoids repeated oscillations by imposing adaptive cooldowns and hydration soft-starts, and (4) exposes observability and runbook steps for on-call teams.
updates: 2026-02-25: Initial proposal written by Leah. Outlined proportional bleed algorithm that weights region egress by SLO headroom (latency p95, error rate, streaming disconnects).

2026-03-01: Architecture review with runtime and gateway teams. Decided telemetry signals: p95 latency, 5xx rate, stream disconnect rate, kv-cache-miss ratio. Added a composite "region health score" to prevent single-signal flips. (Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/PRO-902468).

2026-03-03: Prototype controller implemented in edge-orch service (feature branch: github.com/redwood-inference/edge-orch/pull/389). Prototype simulates gradual bleed steps of 5% every 30s when headroom < threshold. Initial load tests show fewer user-facing disconnects than instant failover, but increased TTL syncing on backend caches.
2026-03-06: PM feedback (Marco Silva): ensure bounded customer impact during long degradations and add opt-in immediate cutover action for SES incidents. Added canary policy with operator override.

2026-03-08: Design review flagged risk of oscillation when hydration reintroduces region quickly. Engineering decided on 'circuit hydration'—a staged reinstatement with token-preserving handshake, KV lease catchup, and progressive load acceptance (1%, 5%, 20%, 50%, 100%) with increasing success gates. Added adaptive cooldown that lengthens with repeated failures.

2026-03-10: Streaming UX edge-case: long-lived sessions with server-streaming must not replay tokens. Implemented ephemeral-proxy handshake where a new region proxy streams while old proxy drains; token continuity validated via checksum.
2026-03-12: Observability added to Grafana: slo-overview panel, region-health heatmap, evacuation-simulation dashboard. Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/edge/slo-overview?orgId=1

2026-03-14: Security notes: KMS access required for ephemeral proxy tokens; raised security review. Draft runbook created for oncall (Confluence runbook link added). PR for controller adjustments awaiting review (github.com/redwood-inference/edge-orch/pull/4289).
acceptance_criteria: Evacuation controller can reduce regional egress in fine-grained steps and finish a full evacuation without an immediate mass reconnect in >95% of simulated degradations.
Session continuity: <=0.1% of active streaming sessions dropped as a result of controller-driven shifts in load tests that match production traffic shape.
SLO protection: 95th latency and error-rate SLOs are preserved in non-degraded regions and system-level SLO compliance does not drop below 99.5% during controlled evacuations.

No oscillation: circuit hydration cooldown prevents region re-enable cycles shorter than configured min_cooldown (default 10m), and repeated failures increase cooldown exponentially up to max_cooldown.
Observability: New Grafana panels and alert rules (paged) present clear signals: region health, evaporation progress, failed hydration attempts, and customer-impact estimation.
Runbook: On-call runbook reviewed and approved by SRE and PM with explicit manual override steps and safe rollback instructions.

Add region health composite signal and tunable thresholds (Telemetry team).
Design and implement circuit hydration protocol with token-preserving handshake and KV lease catchup (Runtime team).
Implement ephemeral proxy drain/handshake for streaming sessions (Gateway team).
Add Grafana dashboards and alerting rules, tie to pager duty runbook (SRE).
Integration testing: chaos engineer runbook + load-test scenarios (QA/Perf).
Security review for ephemeral token usage and KMS calls (Security).
Documentation: Confluence design doc, runbook, and release notes (Documentation/PM).
